A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowVerse benchmark and MathFlow pipeline. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, MathFlow experiments, component ablations, error analyses and qualitative comparisons, including MathVision results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds extraction-quality, image-only, sensitivity and efficiency results.

M1.justification: The perception-to-text-to-inference pipeline and two-stage MathFlow-P-7B training procedure remain unchanged. Renaming RP captioning as visual-oriented reasoning and evaluating alternative backbones do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an image-only scenario by rendering question text onto diagrams, changing the input conditions for five FlowVerse variants. Existing mathematical domains, languages and benchmark datasets remain represented; MathVision moves from v1's appendix to v2's main text.

E2.justification: The FlowVerse comparison adds GPT-5, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, VLM-R1-7B, Math-LLaVA, MultiMath and SVE-Math. SPHINX-MoE and InternLM-XC2 disappear from the full FlowVerse comparison while remaining elsewhere. New extraction and perception-model comparisons, including mPLUG-Doc variants, substantially expand the comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces exact-set EI/RP F1 evaluation on a curated FlowVerse subset, an alpha sweep over 0.2–0.8, and accuracy/latency comparisons across 3B–72B configurations with end-to-end and untrained-pipeline controls. These substantially expand the evaluation design beyond the retained benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: New analyses examine extraction quality, alternative perception models, scoring-weight sensitivity, image-only robustness and reasoning efficiency (v2 Tables 5, 7 and 16–18). Earlier EI/RP ablations, error analyses and qualitative cases are retained, including material relocated to the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions for the CoT-evaluator comparison and display error bars in Figure 5. v2 introduces no additional seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including MathFlow-P-7B EI/RP F1 scores of 97.2%/85.6%, new baseline scores, image-only outcomes and latency measurements. Existing FlowVerse values also change: GPT-4V's Table 1 All CoT-E/Acc changes from 64.2/58.7 to 56.2/53.4. The PDFs do not explain whether these revisions reflect corrections or new runs; MathVerse Table 2 remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The FlowVerse-CoT-E scoring equation remains unchanged. v2's added precision, recall and F1 equations explain standard evaluation formulas; they introduce no substantive theoretical derivation, formal assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: FlowVerse, a modular perception/inference pipeline, and MathFlow-P-7B improving visual mathematical reasoning with different inference models. The additional experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands RP's interpretation as a diagnostic variable separating property generation from utilization, and adds interpretations concerning sensitivity, efficiency and inspectable intermediate outputs. The difficulty and language limitations are relocated, but v1's warning that the perception model's reasoning remains basic is removed.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler, beta values, weight decay and explicit GeoGPT4V training-source identification. It newly discloses multiple reference solutions for eligible questions. These are documentation changes; actual changes to the optimizer or training-data composition are not established.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed from visual instruction tuning and dataset construction toward visual mathematical reasoning, tools, test-time scaling and reinforcement learning. Added discussions cite works such as Describe-then-Reason, Slow Perception, VisuoThink and Skywork R1V2, while much of the earlier instruction-tuning survey is removed.

P1.justification: v2 separates FlowVerse and MathFlow into standalone sections, rewrites related work, creates a dedicated ablation section, moves limitations into the main text and reorganizes the appendix around datasets and experiments with a contents list. RP explanations and several narrative passages are also substantially revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds five analysis tables, restructures FlowVerse tables into model groups, redraws the benchmark schematic and charts, and changes table highlighting and document layout. MathVision's table moves into the main text, while the earlier problem-solving example moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: New extraction-quality, robustness and efficiency studies address gaps in v1. However, v2 adds MathFlow rows to Table 1 while Section 5.2 still says it is excluded, and Section 5.3 credits GPT-5 with cross-dataset superiority absent from the cited Table 4. These inconsistencies, unexplained score revisions and removed training details make the reliability of the expanded evidence uncertain, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
